behaviour: C1: PollVotePayload carries optional `seq` (non-negative safe integer); parsePollVote rejects any other present value; absent = legacy = seq 0.
C2: isNewerVote orders votes by (seq, created_at, rumorId) with legacy seq 0 / rumorId ''; strict total order.

C3: every vote write (handleVote, early-vote replay, castVote, journal replay via handleVote) goes through saveVoteIfNewer, a compare-and-set inside pollPersistence's per-key write queue; the plain upsert saveVote no longer exists.
C4: queuePendingVote keeps the newer entry by the comparator; replayPendingVotes relies on the CAS (no votedAt skip).
C5: castVote derives seq = max(stored own seq, own queued seq, 0) + 1, serialised per (group, poll); stores votedAt/rumorId of the sent rumor; optimistic UI update applies the comparator.

C6: a close for an unknown poll is queued per (group, poll, authenticated closer), first kept, <=10 polls per sender per group, <=50 per group oldest evicted, 7-day TTL, persisted; applied on the poll-open's new-poll path after the early-vote replay only when closer == authenticated creator (case-insensitive), else discarded.

C7: a poll_close chat announcement for an unknown poll is queued the same way (rumor id, sender, created_at) and re-run through the same chat gate after the open; never appended for a non-creator; a lookup failure still rejects (fail closed).
C8: AC-9 amended, docs/behavior/polls.md updated, pollReplay.ts doc comment updated.
non_goals: No new e2e spec (MLS reordering cannot be forced through the app).
No migration rewriting stored votes to carry seq (legacy rows rank as seq 0 at read time).
No change to the dispatcher, the rumor journal, or closePoll's local tally.
Applying a pending close on a re-delivered open of an already-known poll (design: new-poll path only).
deviations_from_design: Pending-close (and announcement) queue entries are keyed per (group, poll, sender) instead of per (group, poll): with first-kept per poll, a member who forged a close for a not-yet-opened poll id would occupy the slot and the creator's genuine close would be dropped. Per-sender keying keeps every bound of the design (one entry per poll per sender, <=10 per sender, <=50 per group).
